description: Chat completions end to end: the OpenAI-compatible front (horde-oai) traffic, a front-to-horde funnel, delivery parity between streamed and stored replies, latency, capacity and wake sources from app OTLP metrics on mimir-telemetry; the horde's native chat routes, chat return codes and worker progress posts; the front's finished-request log line on loki-app; and chat traces in Tempo.

panels.title: Front traffic (OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions)

panels.description: Chat requests that took an in-flight slot over the dashboard range. Source: horde.oai.requests.admitted.
panels.title: Admitted

panels.description: Completions delivered to the client over the range. Source: horde.oai.completions.
panels.title: Completions delivered

panels.description: Completions divided by admitted requests over the range. Client disconnects, timeouts, horde refusals and faults all lower it.
panels.title: Delivered share of admitted

panels.description: Requests refused before taking an in-flight slot: body size or read timeout, validation, authorization, front at capacity.
panels.title: Refused before admission

panels.description: Admitted requests answered with an error status before any header: horde refusals at submit, timeouts, no eligible worker, faults, horde unavailable.
panels.title: Errors after admission

panels.description: Streamed requests whose 200 headers were sent and which then ended in an SSE error event.
panels.title: Stream failures after headers

panels.description: Admitted requests by streamed flag, and completions delivered.
panels.title: Admitted and delivered per minute

panels.description: Completions by the model a worker served. 'usage estimated' counts completions whose token usage the front estimated because the worker did not report it.
panels.title: Delivered completions per minute, by model

panels.description: Cancels the front sent to the horde, by outcome, and requests carrying an SDK retry count above zero (clients retrying after an error). acknowledged: the horde accepted the cancel. already_gone: the horde no longer holds the request, so the cancel is not retried. failed, timed_out and not_started (no cancel slot came free in time, so nothing was sent) are retried periodically until the cancel expires. Each attempt is counted, so a cancel retried several times appears once per attempt.
panels.title: Cancels and client retries per minute

panels.description: Refusals before an in-flight slot. FrontAtCapacity (503) means the front's global or per-source cap was reached.
panels.title: Refused before admission per minute, by status and code

panels.description: Admitted requests that ended in an error status before any header. '(none)' is a status without a code, such as a 429 passed through from the horde. reason splits a queue refusal into no_eligible_threads (no online worker can serve it) and wait_exceeds_budget (the estimated wait is longer than the request may wait); other errors show '(none)'.
panels.title: Errors after admission per minute, by status, code and reason

panels.description: Streams that ended in an SSE error event after 200 headers.
panels.title: Stream failures per minute, by code

panels.description: Every admitted request by final code, HTTP status and streamed flag. A stream records status 200 whatever its outcome; 'ok' is a delivered completion and 'client_closed' a client that disconnected first.
panels.title: Request outcomes over the range

panels.description: Requests refused before an in-flight slot, by code and status.
panels.title: Refusals before admission over the range
Chat funnel (front and horde)

panels.description: Each stage of a chat request per minute. Arrived, admitted, relaying, delivered, errored and stream failures are the OpenAI-compatible front's counts. Created and assigned are the horde's counts for every chat request, front and native API together, so they can exceed the front's stages. Created excludes requests refused for want of kudos. Rare stages are drawn as zero until their first event.
panels.title: Chat funnel per minute

panels.description: Completions divided by every request that reached the front, refused ones included, over the range. Shows COLLECTING below 20 arrivals.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(horde_oai_completions{job="ai-horde/horde-oai", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment"}[$__range])) / clamp_min((sum(increase(horde_oai_requests_admitted{job="ai-horde/horde-oai", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment"}[$__range])) + (sum(increase(horde_oai_requests_refused{job="ai-horde/horde-oai", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment"}[$__range])) or vector(0))), 1)) and on() ((sum(increase(horde_oai_requests_admitted{job="ai-horde/horde-oai", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment"}[$__range])) + (sum(increase(horde_oai_requests_refused{job="ai-horde/horde-oai", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment"}[$__range])) or vector(0))) >= 20)

panels.title: Delivered of arrived

panels.description: Chat requests assigned to a worker divided by chat requests created on the horde over the range. A low share means requests expire or are cancelled before any worker takes them. Shows COLLECTING below 20 created.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(horde_text_queue_wait_seconds_count{job="ai-horde/ai-horde", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", horde_chat="true"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum(increase(horde_text_free_allowance_decisions{job="ai-horde/ai-horde", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", horde_chat="true", horde_outcome!="refused"}[$__range])), 1)) and on() (sum(increase(horde_text_free_allowance_decisions{job="ai-horde/ai-horde", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", horde_chat="true", horde_outcome!="refused"}[$__range])) >= 20)

panels.title: Assigned of created (horde)
Delivery parity (streamed against stored replies)

panels.description: How streams that relayed worker progress ended. equal and prefix are consistent with the stored reply; mismatch, replaced_attempt, ended and gap ended the stream with an error event.
panels.title: Relay outcomes per hour

panels.description: Relayed streams that ended in mismatch, replaced_attempt or gap, over all relayed streams in the range. Green below 1%, red from 5%. Shows COLLECTING below 20 relayed streams.
panels.title: Relay divergence share

panels.description: Delivered completions whose token usage was estimated rather than reported by the worker.
panels.title: Estimated usage share

panels.description: Delivered completions holding a generation without visible text, over the range.
panels.title: Empty completions

panels.description: Requests answered with submit_outcome unknown over the range: the front could not tell whether the horde accepted the submit.
panels.title: Unknown submit outcomes

panels.description: Submits the front re-sent after losing the answer, by whether the horde found an existing claim for the operation key, and requests answered with an unknown submit outcome.
panels.title: Lost submits per hour

panels.description: Wakes whose status read found the request done, not faulted and without a finished generation. The front keeps waiting on these, so a steady rate means requests end without a reply.
panels.title: Status reads finding a request done without a generation, per minute
Reasoning and completion content

panels.description: What the first generation of each delivered completion holds: text (visible content), tool_calls, reasoning_only (no visible content, reasoning) or empty. Whitespace is not visible content.
panels.title: Delivered completions per minute, by content

panels.description: Delivered completions that were reasoning_only or empty, 1-hour window. reasoning_only with finish reason length is a reply whose limit went to reasoning; the client cannot resume it.
panels.title: Completions without visible text per hour, by content and finish reason

panels.description: reasoning_only and empty completions over all completions that carry the content label, over the range.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(horde_oai_completions{job="ai-horde/horde-oai", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", horde_model=~"$model", horde_content=~"reasoning_only|empty"}[$__range])) or on() vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(increase(horde_oai_completions{job="ai-horde/horde-oai", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", horde_model=~"$model", horde_content!=""}[$__range])), 1)

panels.title: No visible text share

panels.description: Completions over the range that held only reasoning and stopped at the limit (finish reason length).

targets.expr: sum(increase(horde_oai_completions{job="ai-horde/horde-oai", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", horde_model=~"$model", horde_content="reasoning_only", horde_finish_reason="length"}[$__range])) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: Lost to reasoning

panels.description: Reasoning tokens over completion tokens for each delivered completion with reasoning, 1-hour window. Either count may be estimated. A share near 1 with finish reason length is a reply whose budget went to reasoning.
panels.title: Reasoning share of completion tokens p50 / p95, by finish reason

panels.description: The reasoning_effort the client sent, or 'omitted'.
panels.title: Delivered completions per minute, by reasoning effort

panels.description: The max_tokens each request accepted by the horde ran under, 1-hour window. client: sent by the client; default: not sent, so 512; lowered: lowered to the largest limit an online worker declares. Not split by model, so the Model variable does not apply.
panels.title: Completion limit p50 / p95, by source

panels.description: Requests the horde accepted at submit, by where their max_tokens came from. A request that ended before any status read is counted as client or default even if the limit was lowered.
panels.title: Accepted requests per minute, by limit source

panels.description: Admitted requests that got an error status before any header, by the upper bound of the max_tokens bucket the request asked for ('over' is above 16384).
panels.title: Errors after admission over the range, by code and max_tokens bucket
Front latency

panels.description: From an admitted request's arrival to its end, including the wait for a worker. A streamed request lasts until its stream ends.
panels.title: Request duration p50 / p95, by streamed and status

panels.description: From the submit acknowledgement to the first content sent: the first completion chunk, or the non-streamed body. relayed=true is a stream whose first content was a progress delta relayed while the worker generated.
panels.title: Time to first content p50 / p95, by streamed and relayed

panels.description: The horde's queue_wait_seconds of each delivered generation: request creation to assignment to a worker.
panels.title: Queue wait p50 / p95, by model

panels.description: Latency of each call from the front to the horde's native API, from taking a call slot to the answer. 'refused' is a horde status of 400 or above; 'abandoned' means the request's budget ended first.
panels.title: Native call duration p95, by call type and outcome

panels.description: Calls from the front to the horde's native API. Status reads dominate while requests wait.
panels.title: Native calls per second, by call type and outcome

panels.description: Size of each request body received whole. Oversized bodies are counted as refusals instead.
panels.title: Request body size p50 / p95

panels.description: Server-side duration from the front's HTTP instrumentation (milliseconds). Requests to unknown paths carry no route.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, http_method, http_target, http_status_code) (rate(http_server_duration_bucket{job="ai-horde/horde-oai", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment"}[5m])))

panels.title: Front HTTP p95, by route and status

panels.description: Client-side duration of the front's HTTP calls to the horde (milliseconds), from the HTTP client instrumentation.
panels.title: Front calls to the horde p95, by method and status
Front capacity

panels.description: Requests holding an in-flight slot. The dashed line is the front's default global cap (1000); a deployment can set another.
panels.title: Requests holding an in-flight slot

panels.description: Distinct client addresses holding at least one slot, and the most slots one address holds. The dashed line is the default per-source cap (5); a deployment can set another.

targets.legendFormat: slots held by the busiest address

panels.title: Distinct sources and the busiest source

panels.description: Requests the front's HTTP server is handling, including streams still open.
panels.title: Active HTTP requests in the front server, by method

panels.description: FrontAtCapacity (503, refused before admission) when the front's global or per-source in-flight cap is reached, and ChatRequestTimeout (408, after admission) when a request reaches its time budget without a result. Both responses carry Retry-After. Front counters only appear after their first event, so a quiet front shows no series.
panels.title: Capacity refusals and request timeouts per minute

panels.description: All responses of the front's HTTP server.
panels.title: Front HTTP responses per second, by route and status

panels.description: The front's HTTP calls to the horde: POST submits, GET status reads and models, DELETE cancels.
panels.title: Front calls to the horde per second, by method and status
Wake sources (how waiting requests learn they finished)

panels.description: Each status read of a waiting request by its cause: immediate (after the submit), signal, recheck, poll, deadline; and disconnect, recorded without a read.
panels.title: Status reads per minute, by wake source

panels.description: Of the status reads that found the request finished, the share per wake source. A high poll share means the completion signal is not reaching the front.

targets.expr: sum by (horde_wake_source) (rate(horde_oai_wakes{job="ai-horde/horde-oai", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", horde_found_finished="true"}[5m])) / ignoring (horde_wake_source) group_left sum(rate(horde_oai_wakes{job="ai-horde/horde-oai", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", horde_found_finished="true"}[5m]))

panels.title: Share of finishes found, by wake source

panels.description: Share of finished requests found through the completion signal over the range.
panels.title: Finishes found by signal
Horde native chat API (/api/v2/generate/chat)

panels.description: Requests to the horde's native chat routes, from every client including the front.
panels.title: Chat route requests per second, by route and status

panels.description: Server-side duration of the native chat routes (milliseconds).
panels.title: Chat route latency p50 / p95, by route

panels.description: Share of chat route responses with a 5xx status. Absent when there were none.

targets.expr: sum by (http_target) (rate(http_server_duration_count{job="ai-horde/ai-horde", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", http_target=~"/api/v2/generate/chat/.*", http_status_code=~"5.."}[5m])) / clamp_min(sum by (http_target) (rate(http_server_duration_count{job="ai-horde/ai-horde", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", http_target=~"/api/v2/generate/chat/.*"}[5m])), 1e-9)

panels.title: Chat route 5xx share, by route

panels.description: Refusals on the chat routes, plus chat return codes on any route (for example a worker's chat reply refused at text submit).

targets.expr: sum by (horde_rc, http_route, http_response_status_code) (increase(horde_api_rejections{job="ai-horde/ai-horde", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", http_route=~"/api/v2/generate/chat/.*"}[$__range])) or sum by (horde_rc, http_route, http_response_status_code) (increase(horde_api_rejections{job="ai-horde/ai-horde", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", horde_rc=~".*Chat.*"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Chat refusals by return code over the range

panels.description: Chat replies the horde refused when a worker submitted them: ChatSubmitInvalid (no client could use it), ChatSubmitNonconformant (broke a strict request's tool_choice or response_format) and ChatModelMismatch (a model other than the one popped). ChatJobAborted answers a progress post for a generation that was already aborted, which tells the worker to stop. Per-worker counts are on the text worker dashboards.
panels.title: Worker chat replies and progress posts refused, per minute
Worker progress and conformance

panels.description: Worker progress posts on /api/v2/generate/text/progress. accepted and duplicate are normal; gap, over_cap and forbidden are refused posts; aborted tells the worker to stop; no_lease is a post for a generation that does not stream; unavailable means Redis could not be reached.
panels.title: Progress posts per minute, by outcome

panels.description: Progress posts refused as gap, over_cap or forbidden over all posts in the range. Green below 1%, red from 5%. Shows COLLECTING below 50 posts.
panels.title: Refused progress share

panels.description: Progress posts made with an API key that does not own the generation's worker, over the range.
panels.title: Forbidden progress posts

panels.description: Pops by a chat worker whose measured speed does not finish the chat output it declares inside the base lease, so longer chat requests reach it only when no capable chat worker is online, and pop skips for the chat filters (lease_speed, chat_jobs, chat_features).
panels.title: Speed-limited chat pops and chat skip reasons per minute

panels.description: Stored chat replies holding the reasoning-budget marker, 1-hour window. reasoning is the budget closing the reasoning as intended. content (the marker in the visible reply) and open_think (a reply starting with an unsplit think block) are worker-side defects.
panels.title: Reasoning budget markers per hour, by place

panels.description: Stored chat replies holding the reasoning-budget marker, by model and where it appears.
panels.title: Reasoning budget markers over the range, by model and place

panels.description: Chat jobs popped whose client did not send reasoning_effort, 1-hour window. applied=true: the worker declares the feature and received medium. applied=false: the worker does not declare it, so its reasoning has no budget from the horde.
panels.title: Chat pops without reasoning_effort per hour, by applied
Finished-request log (front)

panels.description: One 'Chat request ... finished:' line per admitted request, parsed. woke_by is the wake source of the read that found the request finished; None for a timeout, fail-fast or horde error. Filter with $code and $host.

targets.expr: sum by (code, woke_by, streamed) (count_over_time({app="ai-horde", component="oai", instance=~"$host"} |= "finished: streamed=" | regexp "streamed=(?P<streamed>\\S+) .* woke_by=(?P<woke_by>\\S+) .* code=(?P<code>\\S+)" | code=~"$code" [$__range]))

panels.title: Finished requests by code, wake source and streamed

panels.description: The front's finished-request line. Use the Code variable to pick outcomes; the line carries no key, prompt, title or client address.
panels.title: Finished-request lines

panels.description: Lines the horde writes for chat refusals (the return code, then the reason; this includes worker replies refused at submit) and chat warnings such as failed image or fault-reason storage.
panels.title: Horde chat refusals and warnings
Traces

panels.description: Root spans of chat requests at the front, newest first. Open a trace to see the horde's spans beneath. Trace retention is short; keep ranges within a day.
panels.title: Recent chat requests

panels.description: Chat requests that took over 30 seconds or ended with an error status.
panels.title: Slow or failed chat requests
